newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European stocks fall as confidence undermined.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European stocks fall as confidence undermined.

text.p: European bourses fell on on Monday as a weakening dollar ate away at investor optimism engendered by Wall Street's rally on Friday.

The dollar lost a pfennig with traders anxiously awaiting a batch of German figures this week. The data could signal returning strength to the German economy, which would be good news for the mark against the dollar.

The lacklustre showing in equity markets came despite a dramatic turnaround on Friday which saw London, Frankfurt and Paris ending with gains as U.S. economic data eased worries about an early rise in interest rates.
In London, Europe's biggest bourse, stocks were weak because the shares of a large batch of companies were diluted as they were declared ex-dividend.
London's FTSE 100 index was down 0.8 percent points by lunch-time as major companies such as Wellcome, HSBC and B.A.T Industries went ex-dividend.

The market was little moved initially by the government's announcement of a May 1 election but analysts said attention was likely to focus in the coming weeks on the lengthy election campaign and opinion polls.
Strategists said the markets should already have discounted the polls and a likely win for the opposition Labour party, but added that a short-term fall was still on the cards.
The Labour party, high in opinion polls, is traditionally seen as less friendly to business interests.
"There is talk of issues such as higher corporation taxes under Labour but there will be delight (once) the election has been called," said one senior trader.
In Frankfurt, floor trade lost early gains to show a slight loss by midday, unable to build on Friday's rally.
Dealers blamed the falling dollar which dimmed export prospects. The computerised IBIS index was down by over 1.5 percent in the early afternoon.
"There's nothing to trade on at the moment. The dollar is softer but not greatly changed, and Bunds (government bonds) are pretty steady," said one dealer.
Paris was hit badly by the downturn in sentiment. The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down over over 1.5 percent at the end of the morning session.
Traders said investors were worried about the volatility of the markets and trade was likely to be cautious before U.S. housing starts data on Tuesday and inflation on Wednesday.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 38.85 points at 2,606.77, while the CAC-40 March futures contract was 22 points lower at 2,618.
"I'm expecting the market to consolidate down to 2,550 points," after its recent gains, said Olivier Blitz at IFF Bourse.
On currency markets, the dollar fell sharply against the mark and but recovered most early losses against the yen.

"Dollar/mark is going through a bit of a clear-out at the moment, there's no news driving it and people are generally still looking for a firmer dollar in the medium-term," said a Japanese bank dealer.

Many traders were awaiting word on American interest rates which could come from the next U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on March 25. Opinion is divided over what action the Fed will take.
The main focus for this week was on German economic data later this week which includes the February IFO business climate survey, February M3 money supply and German CPI data.
The data will be eyed closely for any sign of returning strength to the German economy which will be mark supportive.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6875 marks and 123.43 yen, compared with Friday's late European levels of 1.6972 marks and 123.45 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 39.4 points at 4,384.9.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 38.85 points at 2,606.77.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 5.71 points at 3,353.58.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $352.05 an ounce, compared with $352.75 at the close on Friday. Silver was at $5.26, compared with $5.31 on Friday.
